what: Bristol Myers Squibb develops and sells prescription medicines, concentrated in cancer, blood disorders, immunology, heart disease and brain disorders. Its best-known products include the blood thinner Eliquis and the cancer immunotherapy Opdivo.
customers: Health systems, insurers and government payers, with medicines prescribed by specialists.
money: newer medicines including Opdivo, Reblozyl, Breyanzi, Camzyos and Cobenfy
Eliquis, Revlimid and Pomalyst, which face or will face generic competition
moat: Patents, large late-stage trial capability and manufacturing for complex biologics and cell therapies that few companies can run.
risks: Eliquis and Revlimid, two of its largest products, lose exclusivity and revenue will fall sharply
US Medicare price negotiation already covers Eliquis
Debt of about $45 billion was raised partly for acquisitions
The newer portfolio must grow fast enough to replace the losses
opportunities: Cobenfy is the first genuinely new mechanism for schizophrenia in decades and addresses a large unmet need
Camzyos and Reblozyl are growing quickly from a small base
A dividend yield above 4% is paid while the portfolio turns over
watch: Whether growth-portfolio revenue rises faster than the legacy portfolio falls, and Cobenfy prescriptions.
